name: research_benchmark_v1
description: Standardized benchmark suite for evaluating end-to-end AI research agent quality across planning, retrieval, grounding, citation integrity, and latency.

cases.question: What are the primary technical bottlenecks preventing commercial-scale net-gain fusion power?
reference_facts: Commercial D-T fusion requires breeding tritium using lithium blankets.
14 MeV high-energy neutrons cause severe material displacement damage in the first wall.

cases.question: How do mRNA vaccines elicit immunological memory compared to traditional attenuated viral vaccines?
reference_facts: mRNA vaccines deliver instructions via lipid nanoparticles to translate target antigens intracellularly.
Both CD4+ helper and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells are stimulated alongside germinal center B-cell responses.

cases.question: What are the biological mechanisms of cellular senescence and how does it contribute to mammalian aging?
reference_facts: Senescent cells undergo irreversible cell-cycle arrest driven by p53/p21 and p16 pathways.
The senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) releases pro-inflammatory cytokines damaging surrounding tissue.

cases.question: What are the comparative trade-offs between dense Transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures during inference?
reference_facts: MoE models activate only a subset of parameters per token, reducing FLOPs relative to total parameter count.
MoE requires full model weights in VRAM, increasing memory bandwidth demands during autoregressive generation.

cases.question: What mechanisms cause catastrophic forgetting in continual learning for large neural models and what are modern mitigations?
reference_facts: Backpropagation optimizes weights for new task objectives, overwriting representations learned for previous tasks.
Mitigations include episodic rehearsal buffers, regularization techniques, and modular parameter adapters.

cases.question: How does Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) differ mathematically and operationally from RLHF with PPO?
reference_facts: DPO derives an analytical formulation expressing reward directly via the policy's log-ratio against a reference model.
DPO bypasses explicit reward model fitting and actor-critic reinforcement learning loops.

cases.question: What are the performance and consistency trade-offs of Raft vs Multi-Paxos in distributed key-value stores?
reference_facts: Raft enforces a strong leader where log entries only flow from the leader to followers.
Multi-Paxos allows more flexible pipelining but has higher protocol and state-machine complexity.

cases.question: How does memory safety in Rust differ from garbage collection in Go regarding latency unpredictability and CPU overhead?
reference_facts: Rust enforces memory safety at compile time using ownership and borrowing with zero runtime GC pauses.
Go uses a concurrent tri-color mark-and-sweep garbage collector optimized for sub-millisecond stop-the-world pauses.

cases.question: What architectural patterns effectively mitigate cascading failures in distributed microservice architectures?
reference_facts: Circuit breakers trip when error thresholds are exceeded, preventing unconstrained caller thread exhaustion.
Load shedding and backpressure drop low-priority traffic before queue delays degrade downstream services.

cases.question: What are the fundamental physical and architectural limitations of scaling silicon DRAM below 10 nanometers?
reference_facts: Scaling DRAM cell capacitors below 10nm causes excessive leakage current and aspect-ratio manufacturing limits.
Cell-to-cell capacitive coupling increases disturbance errors, aggravating Rowhammer vulnerabilities.

cases.question: How do modern solid-state batteries differ from conventional lithium-ion cells regarding energy density, cycle life, and dendrite formation?
reference_facts: Solid-state batteries replace flammable liquid electrolytes with solid ceramics, sulfides, or polymers.
Using pure lithium metal anodes drastically increases energy density, but requires preventing dendritic short circuits.

cases.question: What is the operating principle of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography and why does it require reflective optics?
reference_facts: 13.5 nm EUV radiation is absorbed by almost all matter, including air and optical glass.
EUV requires reflective molybdenum-silicon multilayer Bragg mirrors in a vacuum chamber.

cases.question: What were the primary geological and climatological factors that caused the Younger Dryas cooling event?
reference_facts: A catastrophic release of freshwater from proglacial Lake Agassiz freshened North Atlantic surface waters.
The influx disrupted the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), causing rapid regional cooling.

cases.question: What are the leading hypotheses regarding the causes of the Late Bronze Age collapse in the Eastern Mediterranean?
reference_facts: The collapse around 1200 BCE affected the Mycenaeans, Hittites, and Levantine coastal cities.
Modern consensus favors a complex systems collapse combining drought, invasions by the Sea Peoples, and disruptions of vital tin trade routes.

cases.question: How did the 1987 Montreal Protocol achieve global phase-out of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and what made its enforcement effective?
reference_facts: CFCs catalyze ozone destruction in the stratosphere via chlorine free radicals.
The protocol incorporated trade restrictions against non-signatories and a Multilateral Fund aiding developing nations.
